title: Self-governing: the lint carries the state
html:
English | Português (Brasil)

Self-governing: the lint carries the state

In tutorial 04, the golmet validate checked the whole RN-001 cycle and came out green. This page explains the philosophy behind those checks — and why Golmet works where traditional processes rot.

The principle

The AI does not carry the whole state; the lint carries it — and the AI fixes what the lint points at. It sounds inverted, but it is what makes the system operate: the lint (golmet lint) is a deterministic sweep — same tree, same output, no judgment. It points at exactly what is broken, with the remediation citing the skill responsible for the fix. No agent needs to re-derive the project's state; nobody needs to remember to check anything.

The two levels — and what they watch

The hard level is golmet validate: the FORMAT's H1–H10 rules block — a Feature is never born from a PEND (H1), a ready Feature requires an active RN (H3), an active RN requires evidence (H4), the evidence resolves in the code (H7), cross-references resolve (H10), the index state is immutable history (H8). That is what blocks the merge.

The soft level is the rest: the doctor's S1–S5 warnings (stale evidence, missing capabilities with declared degradation) and the lint L1–L10 — the docs' dead refs (L1), orphans without provenance (L3), stale manifest entries (L4), names off the standard (L5), cited ghost gm-* components (L6), the canonical structure (L7), aggregate sizes (L7-size), the definitive↔template conformance (L8), the registries schema (L9) and the state packs' internal state (L10). None of it blocks on its own — but everything shows up, always.

Where it runs

The lint runs in the kit repo's CI (a doc with a dead ref = broken build), via MCP (gm_lint — read-only for the agents), at the maintenance skills' gates (gm-setup validates post-install, gm-workflow-improver requires a green lint post-fix, the gm-pack-* validate post publish/update). The golmet validate is the everyday gate — and --json is the contract for CI and agents.

The practical consequence: MeuApp's documentation stays correct not because someone has discipline — because deviating from it is the hard path.
